title: Tanzanian Grilled Fish Tamarind Glaze
community: Tanzanian fine dining — hotel and restaurant signature
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Tanzanian Tamarind Glazed Fish — whole red snapper or sea bream roasted with a Zanzibar spice rub, finished with a tamarind-honey-ginger glaze that caramelises magnificently. Served with coconut jasmine rice and sautéed local greens. The hotel restaurant signature — elevated traditional flavours presented with fine dining refinement.
longDesc: Tamarind glazed fish is Tanzania's finest hotel dining signature — the technique (roasting then glazing) is classical, but the flavours (Zanzibar spice rub, tamarind-honey glaze, coconut rice) are entirely Tanzanian. This is the dish that demonstrates Tanzanian fine dining's coming of age.
ingredients: 2 whole red snapper (600g each) — scored deeply
// Serve with: coconut jasmine rice, sautéed greens
steps: Mix spice rub ingredients. Rub inside cavities and into score marks of each fish.
Make glaze: combine all glaze ingredients in a small saucepan. Simmer 3 minutes until slightly thickened. Cool.
Roast fish in a hot oven at 200°C for 14—16 minutes.
Remove from oven. Brush generously with glaze.
Return to oven (grill setting) for 3—4 minutes until glaze caramelises.
Rest 3 minutes. Serve with coconut rice and greens.
chefTips: Score the fish deeply — the spice rub penetrates into the score marks.
The glaze goes on at the end — earlier application burns before the fish is cooked.
The grill finish caramelises the glaze — do not skip this step.
Rest the fish — the residual heat continues cooking the centre.
cookingScience: The tamarind's tartaric acid reacts with the honey's natural sugars during glazing to produce a faster, deeper caramelisation than honey alone — the Maillard reaction is accelerated by the pH-lowering effect of the acid. This produces the characteristic mahogany glaze with complex caramelised notes.
sustainabilityTips: Wild-caught Indian Ocean red snapper from local Zanzibar fishermen.
culturalNote: Tanzanian tamarind glazed fish is the dish that Tanzanian hotel chefs present to visiting dignitaries and international guests — the dish that says 'this is what Tanzanian fine dining looks like'. It is Zanzibar's flavour tradition expressed at its most refined.
